source: Song, Lee, Ahn, Sung, Kim (2025) Is a Peeled Apple Still Red? Evaluating LLMs' Ability for Conceptual Combination with Property Type (CCPT)
finding: Closes gap 4. Song et al. measure noun-phrase combination, not blending. They built a dataset of noun phrases, a property, and a property type (emergent, canceled, component, other). Three tasks: property induction (name an emergent or canceled property of a phrase), noun phrase completion (add a modifier so a head noun gains a given emergent property), and property type prediction.
numbers: CCPT: 12,315 annotated triplets (2,501 emergent properties among them). Models: GPT-4o, o1, o1-mini, Sonnet-3.5, Llama-3.1-70B, Qwen2.5-72B. Scores use an LLM judge (GPT-4o) with relevance 0-1; E = emergence score, C = cancellation score. Humans rated 30 sampled items.
quote: LLMs, including OpenAI's o1, struggle to generate noun phrases which possess given emergent properties.
limits: Combination of two nouns plus properties; no blend of distant domains, no generic space, no downstream reasoning task. Judge is GPT-4o, the same family as one tested model.
agent_relevance: Shows the typical failure is leaning on parent properties instead of true emergence. A blend check can test: does the property belong to the merged thing, or only to a parent.

source: Song et al. (2025) CCPT, Table 3 generative results by scaffold
finding: Closes gap 4 (scaffolds). Scaffolds tested: Base prompt, zero-shot Chain-of-Thought, and spreading activation (iterative: retrieve related concepts from the LLM and/or ConceptNet, filter them against the seed concepts, up to T=5 rounds, convergence 0.1, then answer from the expanded concept set), plus a Multi-Oracle best-of-5 upper bound. Spreading activation helps GPT-4o a little; the best-of-5 oracle helps far more.
numbers: GPT-4o, emergent property induction E: Base 40.8, CoT 42.4, SA(LLM) 43.8, SA(ConceptNet) 45.8, SA(both) 45.2, oracle best-of-5 57.8; gold 58.4. GPT-4o noun phrase completion E: Base 20.4, CoT 23.1, SA(LLM) 25.5, SA(ConceptNet) 26.9, SA(both) 26.8, oracle 38.9; human 38.0, gold 59.9. Filter ablation (SA, GPT-4o): canceled 55.6 to 63.3 with filter; emergent 44.6 to 45.8. Iterations C1 to C5 rise from 45.1 to 45.8 (emergent induction). Standard errors across runs are about 0.2 to 2.0 points. Row labels in the pdf extraction were shifted by one row; mapping fixed by the text statement that SA(ConceptNet) exceeds the gold R score by 12.3 (41.5 vs 29.2).
limits: Gains of a few points are only a few standard errors; they are small next to the oracle gap. Token cost of the multi-round loop is not reported. Only one task family. The judge is an LLM.
agent_relevance: A retrieve-then-filter step beats CoT by 2 to 5 points; picking the best of five by a verifier would beat it by 12 to 17. That favours sample-and-verify over a longer scaffold for the blend operator.

source: Song et al. (2025) CCPT, classification task and judge validity
finding: Bears on gaps 3 and 7. GPT-4o can say whether a phrase has a property but often mislabels where the property comes from. This is the peeled-apple error: a property of the parent is kept when the combination cancels it. The LLM judge tracks humans well on this narrow relevance rating.
numbers: GPT-4o: 82.6% accuracy on has-property or not (95.6% on has, 69.6% on does-not-have); only 56.4% on the four-way property type, humans 81% (appendix). Judge vs human relevance rating: Pearson 0.85, Spearman 0.83 (300 pairs, 3 MTurk raters each). Generated emergent properties lean on parents: relatedness to a parent is 12.3 points above gold for the best scaffold.
limits: The task is a single judged property, not a whole blend. Agreement is on a 0 to 1 relevance scale, not valid versus invalid.
agent_relevance: A property-by-property consistency check (does each kept property still hold in the merged thing?) is measurable; a model alone gets the type right only about half the time, so it needs a second look or a code rule.

source: Ismayilzada, Cuomao, Yurshevich, Sotnikova, van der Plas, Bosselut (2026) CresOWLve: benchmarking creative problem-solving over real-world knowledge (COLM 2026)
finding: Bears on gap 2. A downstream benchmark of puzzles that need non-obvious connections between facts (a blend-like step). No blending scaffold was tested. Models retrieve the facts but fail to join them: error analysis says missing creative connection and clue misreading dominate; hallucination and wrong-reference errors are rare.
numbers: 2,061 items, five difficulty levels, English and Russian. Non-thinking models stay under 30% accuracy; GPT-5.4 goes from 9.4% (no thinking) to 17.8% (medium) on the English set, 15.4% to 26.9% Russian. Factual-vs-creative drop of 6.08 points (Gemini-3.1-Pro high) up to 17.21 points (Mistral-Large-3). Strongest thinking models lose over 20 points from very simple to very hard. Every item was solved by expert teams in the original game (implicit human solvability).
limits: Evaluation only: no scaffold, no blend operator, no equal-token comparison. Contamination is possible, especially for Gemini on the Russian set. Judge is GPT-4o with the reference answer.
agent_relevance: A ready test bed for gap 2: run a plain prompt versus a blend-operator prompt on the creative subset, with the factual subset as control.

source: Suzuki and Banaei-Kashani (2026 v3) Universe of Thoughts: a computational framework for creative reasoning in LLMs
finding: Bears on gaps 1, 2 and 10. Combinational UoT (C-UoT) is a coded blend-like operator: pick an external analogue, extract an abstract mechanism, then transfer it back to the target (analogue, mechanism, solution chain). Tested on three new creative reasoning tasks and on HypoArena (100 hypothesis tasks). It is not clearly better than plain prompting or CoT.
numbers: GPT-4o, creativity score (human / LLM judge), Bridge, Electricity, Society: OnePrompt 0.480/0.566, 0.540/0.508, 0.550/0.522; CoT 0.590/0.651, 0.560/0.450, 0.500/0.586; C-UoT 0.580/0.664, 0.440/0.512, 0.560/0.649; T-UoT (transform) 0.680/0.698, 0.620/0.526, 0.550/0.628. Ten generations per cell, 10 PhD raters. HypoArena Qwen3-14B average win rate: E-UoT 32.7, ToT 25.5, CoT 18.8, C-UoT 19.5 (rank 5 of 7), OnePrompt 14.3. Ablation: full C-UoT beats C-UoT without the structured transfer in 58.3% of comparisons (chance 50).
limits: C-UoT is an analogue-mechanism-solution chain, not a generic-space blend with a validity check. Token cost per method not read. Small human cells; judge is a 12B model on HypoArena. By the authors, C-UoT is best only on one low-constraint, low-specificity task.
agent_relevance: First text-only test of a coded combinational operator on solution-seeking tasks: modest, task-dependent, and below exploratory search on hypothesis tasks. Weakens a case for a default blend operator.

source: Suzuki and Banaei-Kashani (2026 v3) Universe of Thoughts, judge agreement tables 8, 11, 12
finding: Bears on gap 7. LLM judges track humans only weakly on creativity at the item level and moderately when averaged over many items. Judges agree with each other moderately.
numbers: Gemini 2.5 Pro vs humans, Pearson: creativity 0.708 at method level (n=27, p=3.6e-5), 0.342 at instance level (n=267); utility 0.481 / 0.249; novelty 0.224 (p=0.26, not significant) / 0.168; feasibility 0.039 / 0.067. HypoArena judges (Gemma, Mistral, Prometheus), Spearman over n=700: 0.616, 0.587, 0.604; exact three-way agreement 0.604, 0.478, 0.520; hard A-B flips 2.6%, 4.4%, 5.4% of 2,100 pairs.
limits: Creativity scoring, not blend validity. Judges from different families but small models.
agent_relevance: Use judge scores to compare methods over many items, not to accept one blend. Novelty from an LLM judge is the least reliable of the four scores.

source: Fu, Conde, Arriaga, Martinez, Reviriego, Coronado-Blazquez (2026) Beyond the Hivemind: escaping LLM homogeneity via meta-persona anchoring and sequential temperature scaling
finding: Bears on gap 6. Within a single model, repeated samples to the same open question are already highly similar: the baseline (top-p 0.9, no persona) is above 0.8 mean pairwise cosine similarity for every model tested. Only the combination of a self-chosen persona and extreme temperature after top-p filtering gets below 0.7. Neither alone does. This is not an exclusion list.
numbers: Intra-model similarity (IRCS), baseline T=1 no persona: Llama-3.1-8B 0.810, Mistral-7B 0.827, Qwen2.5-14B 0.840, Gemma-4-4B 0.858, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-14B 0.880. With persona plus T=32 the paper reports 0.591, 0.570, 0.722, 0.676, 0.625 (cell order from the figure text; assignment of the other cells is ambiguous). Average pairwise cosine 0.85 down to 0.65 overall. Coherence judge (GPT-4o-mini) mean about 7 of 10 at the highest temperature, above 7.5 at T=4. Gains plateau after T=4.
limits: Open prompts (Infinity-Chat), models under 20B, no blend task, no token-matched comparison with an exclusion-list design. Figure cell order in the pdf extraction is ambiguous. One preprint.
agent_relevance: Confirms one model's samples collapse; sampling alone does not fix it. An exclusion list is still untested for blends. Two-stage diversity (anchor first, then sample) is the pattern that worked.

source: Wadhwa, Roy, Lederman, Li, Durrett (2026) CREATE: testing LLMs for associative creativity, prompt-intervention results
finding: Bears on gap 6. On a task of listing many diverse, specific paths between two concepts, telling the model what it already said (iterate: ask for a different answer with prior answers in context) gives the most distinct new paths; plain resampling gives high utility but is blind to earlier outputs. Be-creative and verbalized sampling help little or hurt.
numbers: Interventions: Be creative, Verbalized Sampling, in-context regeneration (iterate), resampling at T=0.7. Iterate and Resample gave the highest creative utility; verbalized sampling returned very few valid or factual paths; creative and original prompts perform very similarly. Nearest-neighbour distance of high-quality paths to the population is similar across models, with iterate highest. Top models by utility: GPT-5.5, Claude-Sonnet-4.6, GPT-5. At patience 1 the best score is about 18 paths. Specific table values are in appendix Tables 19 and 21 and were not copied.
limits: Association paths between entities, not blends. Iterate and Resample use a larger inference budget than the base prompt, so equal tokens is not met, as the authors note. Scores come from an LLM judge (gpt-oss-120b).
agent_relevance: Closest evidence for an exclusion-list memory: showing earlier outputs buys distinctness, but at extra calls. Equal-token test still undone.

source: Wadhwa et al. (2026) CREATE, metric validation against humans
finding: Bears on gap 7. A decomposed LLM judge (specificity and factuality) agrees with humans better than an end-to-end holistic creativity score. The factuality judge over-rejects: high recall of wrong relations but poor precision.
numbers: Specificity: two authors, 75 paths, Krippendorff alpha 0.68; judge vs mean of annotators Pearson 0.67. Factuality: 346 triples, balanced accuracy 85.9%; for incorrect relations recall 0.94 and precision 0.52; for correct relations precision 0.98 and recall 0.77. Overall creative utility: 105 queries, two annotators alpha 0.62, Pearson with the metric 0.51 and 0.48 (average 0.55).
limits: Annotators were the authors, with uneven domain knowledge. Judge is a single open model (gpt-oss-120b); stronger judges checked in appendix.
agent_relevance: Split a blend judgement into small checks (is each property true; is it specific) instead of one good-blend rating. A suspicious verifier (high recall, low precision) fits a retry loop but needs a second pass.

source: Schapiro et al. (2025/2026) Measuring Combinatorial Creativity in LLMs and Humans (KOMBINE), re-opened for failure type, judges and sampling
finding: Bears on gaps 3, 6 and 7. Invalid blends in the failure grid are often subtly wrong generic spaces that sound fine, e.g. a gas-exchange space for bread that fits yeast but not photosynthesis: a coherent-but-wrong case, caught by the judge panel rather than by the model. One sample per item per model at T=0.9, so within-model repeat diversity is not measured. The judge panel mixes three models from two vendors.
numbers: 35 LLMs, T=0.9, top-p and top-k off, default reasoning. Judges: Claude Haiku 4.5, GPT-5.4, o3. Panel ICC(2,3) 0.48 to 0.67 (n=1,023 artifacts). One author blind-checked 60 items (30 analogy, 30 blend), 150 dimension judgments: panel majority agrees 66% of the time; 75% where the panel is unanimous (n=96). On unanimous-only items the ranking correlation with the full board is Spearman 0.945 (n=21). No row of the failure grid is fully invalid: every pair had at least one model with a valid generic space.
limits: The human check was one author on 60 items; no judge from another family was swapped in; no count of how many invalid blends were still coherent.
agent_relevance: Supports a verifier that tests the generic space against BOTH inputs separately (the failure was applies to one input only). Coherent-but-wrong cases are real; their rate for a given model is unmeasured.

source: Zeisler, Shirekar, Lica, Raman (2026) PRISM: a category-theoretic framework for measuring and refining multimodal analogies
finding: Bears on gaps 1 and 8. A different group applies a structure-score verifier plus iterative refinement to visual metaphor generation (not a replication of Xu et al.). Refinement beats zero-shot on metaphor consistency and analogy appropriateness, but the structural score alone is a worse chooser than a zero-shot model.
numbers: AnaloBench story selection: zero-shot GPT-4.1 mini 88.5%; choosing by pullback score alone 82.5% (MRR 0.895, top-2 91.5%). Ablations of the score drop it to 76% and to 24% (chance 25%). Humans prefer the refined image in 57.65% of forced-choice comparisons; refinement raises consistency and appropriateness more than conceptual integration or image quality. Gains are smaller with GPT-6 Astra because its zero-shot scores are higher. A substantial share of items is worse after refinement.
limits: Images, not text reasoning. Claude Sonnet 4.6 and GPT-6 Astra as refiners. Token cost per refinement not read.
agent_relevance: A verifier-in-loop gain exists but is smaller for stronger models and does not beat the plain model as a chooser. Keep retries capped and measure per model.

source: Forward citations of Xu et al. (2026) Beyond pixels (arXiv 2602.01335), Semantic Scholar list pulled this session
finding: Bears on gap 8. Six citing papers were listed. None is a re-run of the staged pipeline against a strong one-shot prompt. Two that mention it (VMetaphor-Bench 2609.02502 and PRISM 2610.01383) were opened: the first says earlier visual-metaphor methods were tested only on small ad hoc sets; the second builds a new method and reuses the evaluation prompts.
numbers: Citers: AdMuse 2610.40190, PRISM 2610.01383, VMetaphor-Bench 2609.02502, 2607.23920, FontCrafter 2603.22054, TAG-MoE 2601.08881. VMetaphor-Bench: 1,500 metaphors, 9,594 multiple-choice questions, 11 text-to-image models, none given the Xu pipeline.
limits: Citation lists are partial and lag; a replication could be under a different name. Authors report about 8.3k tokens and 4 min per sample (earlier pass), cost not independently measured.
agent_relevance: Treat the 3.69 to 4.56 gain as one lab's result. Gap 8 stays open.

source: Eppe et al. (2018) A computational framework for conceptual blending, Artificial Intelligence 256; abstract and forward citations via Semantic Scholar
finding: Bears on gap 5. Publisher PDF again returned an HTML block page; the Pereira and Cardoso optimality-principles pdf returned 404. Only the abstract and the citation list were read. The abstract says generalisation is solved by answer set programming and the blend space is pruned by metrics for optimality principles, shown in maths and music. The citation list has no independent re-implementation. Citing items are mostly formal or application papers.
numbers: 87 citations in Semantic Scholar. Titles seen include A uniform model of computational conceptual blending (2021), Characterising cognitively useful blends (2024), Blending concepts with text-to-image diffusion models (2025), PopBlends (2021), KOMBINE (2025). Pereira and Cardoso, Optimality Principles in Computational Approaches to Conceptual Blending: Do We Need Them (at) All? (2016) exists but was not reachable.
limits: Title-level only: nothing was opened, so replications could hide in citing papers. Guhe 2011, Veale 2019 and the Divago chapters stay unopened.
agent_relevance: No evidence to rely on Divago-style optimality metrics. The part to copy (generalise by search, prune by explicit metrics) is design lore, not a measured gain.

source: Donvito and Lieto (2026) Structural ranking of the cognitive plausibility of computational models of analogy and metaphors with the Minimal Cognitive Grid
finding: Bears on gaps 5 and 10. The TCL authors (Lieto) score their own metaphor model (METCL, a typicality blend) next to SME, CogSketch and LLMs on a rubric. It earns only partial credit: it implements conceptual blending and some inductive reasoning but is not a model of abstraction or general reasoning and cannot be tested on Raven-style items.
numbers: METCL gets 0.5 (of 1) on Fluid Reasoning, 0 on Visual processing; Functional/Structural Ratio for SME and CogSketch 0.65 (METCL value not read). Rubric scoring by the authors, not an experiment.
limits: Not independent: Lieto is a TCL author. A paper-based rubric, no new data. It replicates nothing.
agent_relevance: Even the champion of a typicality blender says it does not reach general reasoning, so it cannot stand in for a reasoning scaffold.

source: Repository sibling files: A09.04 conceptual combination, A11.02 analogical inference, C10.03 candidate inferences, C04.03 combinational creativity (claims.jsonl read this session)
finding: Bears on gap 9. The parallel subfields already hold the better-tested pieces. Analogy-then-solve is the nearest tested operator: A09.04-K25 and A11.02-K29 record a structure-first step that raises novelty at the same number of calls. Candidate-inference checks (one-to-one mapping, grounding rule) are cheap and have human data (A11.02-K03, K04). The combinational creativity file records that finding the shared abstraction is the bottleneck (C04.03-K01) and that archive-based recombination beats fresh sampling at equal compute for executable tasks (C04.03-K27).
numbers: A09.04-K25: novel-solution rate 1.6% (no domain) and 21.6% (cross-domain) up to 50.4% for the staged step at 2 vs 2 calls (as recorded there). A11.02-K29: 50.4 to 68.8% vs 21.6 to 37.9% across three frontier models at call-matched settings. A11.02-K13: analogical prompting about +4% over 0-shot CoT. Numbers copied from sibling claim files, not re-derived here.
limits: Breadth, not validity, is what the call-matched tests measure (A11.02-K29 says so). Sibling statuses vary; I did not re-open their sources.
agent_relevance: Do not build blend-specific machinery first. An analogy-then-solve step plus a grounding and consistency check from the analogy files covers most of the ground; add generic-space-with-verifier only if it beats that.

source: Schapiro, Gladstone, Black, Ji (2026) Assessing the creativity of LLMs: testing, limits and new frontiers (DRAT)
finding: Bears on gap 10 (adjacent, not a blend study). A test mixing remote association with divergent word choice is the only creativity test that significantly predicts scientific ideation quality in LLMs; common tests (DAT, RAT) do not. No test was built around blending.
numbers: DRAT validity rho = +0.57 (p = 0.008) and specificity 0.52 (p = 0.02) for scientific ideation; DRAT vs RAT +0.32 (p<0.05); DRAT vs overall CDAT -0.34. Correlation is across a small number of models.
limits: Across-model correlation on few models; ideation judged by LLMs; no scaffold tested.
agent_relevance: Word-level association tests do not predict idea quality, so a blend-quality rating should not be assumed to transfer to reasoning either.

source: Forward citations of Schapiro et al. (2509.21043) and Song et al. (2502.06086), Semantic Scholar lists
finding: Bears on gaps 5 and 10. KOMBINE has 8 listed citers; CCPT has 2 (KOMBINE and OntoURL). KOMBINE citers: Vocabulary and Verifier Gaps (2607.09560), moral alternatives (2606.31213), cross-domain reasoning for neuromorphic design, Assessing creativity (2605.13450), MoRI (2603.19044), CREATE (2603.09970), Universe of Thoughts (2511.20471), semantic-distance tests. I opened six: none re-runs the 43.4% blend rate; they use KOMBINE as motivation.
numbers: 8 and 2 citers; zero direct re-runs of the blend/analogy/association comparison or of CCPT.
limits: Lists lag. The neuromorphic-design and moral-alternatives papers and the semantic-distance paper were not opened.
agent_relevance: Independent confirmation of the generic-space bottleneck is absent; treat it as a hypothesis for our own test.

source: Chen, Wang, He, Yu, Cao (2026) Blending Concepts: VMetaphor-Bench, benchmarking visual metaphor generation
finding: Bears on gap 10 (image). A benchmark built on blending theory: the model must blend two domains into one picture. Strongest proprietary models still struggle with compositional structure and cross-domain mapping. It tests no scaffold.
numbers: 1,500 visual metaphors, three levels, ten categories; 9,594 multiple-choice questions at four fidelity levels; 11 text-to-image models; MLLM-as-judge.
agent_relevance: No text transfer; supports the view that blend evidence is image-heavy.
